title: Fried-Conte plasma dispersion Z as Faddeeva Hilbert transform of a Maxwellian
expression_sketch: Faddeeva: w(z) := exp(-z**2)*erfc(-I*z). Integral representation, Im(z) > 0: w(z) = (I/pi)*Integral(exp(-t**2)/(z - t), (t, -oo, oo)). Fried-Conte plasma dispersion: Z(z) = I*sqrt(pi)*w(z). Equivalent Fried-Conte definition: Z(zeta) = pi**(-1/2)*Integral(exp(-t**2)/(t - zeta), (t, -oo, oo)) as written for Im(zeta) > 0, and the analytic continuation of that integral for Im(zeta) <= 0. Lower half-plane continuation (Wikipedia Faddeeva): Z(z) = conjugate(Z(conjugate(z))) + 2*I*sqrt(pi)*exp(-z**2) for Im(z) < 0. Real-axis member: Z(x) = pi**(-1/2)*P.Integral(exp(-t**2)/(t - x), t) + I*sqrt(pi)*exp(-x**2). Differential identity: Z'(z) = -2*(1 + z*Z(z)). Entire function of z after continuation.
latent_structure: One entire special function (Faddeeva w / Fried-Conte Z) is the Hilbert-transform master of a Gaussian. The written integral is the Im z > 0 member; Landau continuation to Im z <= 0 (including the 2*i*sqrt(pi)*e^{-z^2} jump) is the same object, not a separate CSE of two real-axis formulae. Linearised Maxwellian plasma permittivity is a specialisation of Z, distinct from the quantum Lindhard occupation divided difference.

z.notes: argument of w and of Z

t.notes: velocity/dummy variable on the real line in the defining integral

function_domains.w: Faddeeva function, entire after the written continuation
function_domains.Z: Fried-Conte plasma dispersion function Z(z) = I*sqrt(pi)*w(z)

nonzero_conditions.statement: The defining integrand has denominator z - t (equivalently t - zeta); the pole sits at t = z
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Faddeeva function, Integral representation: w(z) = (i/pi) Integral exp(-t**2)/(z-t) dt, Im z > 0

analytic_domains.statement: The Faddeeva integral representation is written for Im z > 0
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Faddeeva function, Integral representation: Im z > 0

analytic_domains.statement: Fried and Conte define Z(zeta) as the real-line Gaussian Hilbert integral for Im zeta > 0 and as the analytic continuation of that for Im zeta < 0
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Faddeeva function: Z(z) = i*sqrt(pi)*w(z) 'defined by Fried and Conte, 1961'; Fried and Conte, The Plasma Dispersion Function, Academic Press, 1961, p. 1: defined as written for Im zeta > 0 and as analytic continuation for Im zeta < 0

analytic_domains.statement: Lower-half continuation used for accurate Im(z) < 0 evaluation: Z(z) = conjugate(Z(conjugate(z))) + 2*I*sqrt(pi)*exp(-z**2)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Faddeeva function, Implementations: 'For accurate calculation of Im(z) < 0, one can use Z(z) = [Z(z*)]* + 2 i sqrt(pi) exp[-z**2]'

branch_conventions: Sign in the Hilbert kernel: Wikipedia Faddeeva uses 1/(z-t); Fried-Conte uses 1/(t-zeta). These differ by a minus sign; Z(z) = i*sqrt(pi)*w(z) reconciles them.
Landau contour: the pole is kept above the integration path under analytic continuation (Im zeta decreasing).

limit_domains.statement: J-pole Padé of Z is written as valid in the upper half-plane and for z weakly close to the real axis; the LHP identity is used when Im z < 0
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Wikipedia Faddeeva function, Implementations: Padé 'valid for the upper plane, and z weakly close to the real axis'; LHP identity as above

source_provenance: Fried, B. D. and Conte, S. D., The Plasma Dispersion Function, Academic Press, New York, 1961
Faddeeva, V. N. and Terent'ev, N. N., Tables of values of the function w(z) = exp(-z^2)(1+2i/sqrt(pi)*int_0^z exp(t^2) dt) for complex argument, 1954

derived_conditions.statement: On the real axis the continuation supplies the Landau term I*sqrt(pi)*exp(-x**2) on top of the principal-value Hilbert transform of the Gaussian
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Boundary value of the Im z > 0 integral plus the written LHP jump 2 i sqrt(pi) e^{-z^2}

public_source: Wikipedia, Faddeeva function (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faddeeva_function); Fried and Conte, The Plasma Dispersion Function (Academic Press, 1961).
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE can share e^{-t^2}. LGG antiunifies two Hilbert integrals. The scientific object is one entire Faddeeva/Z master whose Im z > 0 integral and Landau LHP continuation are members, with a written jump 2 i sqrt(pi) e^{-z^2}.
proposer_leak_risk: Do not plant 'Faddeeva', 'Fried-Conte', or 'Landau contour' as gold names. Do not package this as Lindhard occupation DD or as Sokhotski-Plemelj 1/z.
notes: Not Lindhard (ac-r04): that is a Fermi-Dirac Newton quotient of a quantum electron gas. This is the classical Maxwellian Hilbert transform. Not Sokhotski-Plemelj (ac-r02): that is the abstract 1/z boundary value; here the Gaussian weight and entire continuation are the representation. Analytic domain Im z > 0 is written on the Wikipedia integral line, not folklore i epsilon. is_guo=false.
